The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to determine the complete one-loop finite temperature effective action in a direct way, which does not involve the evaluation of any infinite sums, even in the presence of non-trivial backgrounds.

, in contrast to the usual procedure, the finite temperature effective actions are not obtained as the imaginary part of the zero temperature effective actions, but are obtained as the imaginary parts of zero temperature effective actions in a finite temperature background.
the finite temperature effective actions can be used as the starting point for calculating finite temperature amplitudes and, in the process, can be used to check the validity of perturbation theory.
